title: Rectangle Overlap
summary: An axis-aligned rectangle is defined by its bottom-left and top-right corners.
statement: An axis-aligned rectangle is defined by its bottom-left and top-right corners. Two rectangles overlap if their intersection area is positive. Given two rectangles, determine if they overlap by checking if their intersection area is greater than zero.
constraints: Rectangles are [x1,y1,x2,y2] with positive area and axis-aligned.
Touching edges or corners do not count as positive-area overlap.
reference_solution:
def rectangles_overlap(rec1, rec2):
 return max(rec1[0],rec2[0])<min(rec1[2],rec2[2]) and max(rec1[1],rec2[1])<min(rec1[3],rec2[3])
hints: Positive rectangle intersection requires positive overlap on both coordinate axes.
Compare the larger lower bound with the smaller upper bound for x and y.
Strict inequalities exclude zero-width contact while conjunction enforces two-dimensional area.
editorial: Strict inequalities exclude zero-width contact while conjunction enforces two-dimensional area.

tests.explanation: Both axis projections overlap with positive length.
The rectangles only share an edge, so they do not overlap.
